TUESDAY MORNING WEATHER
(Powered By: Rose City Air & Project One Roofing) 

Good Tuesday morning! The rainy days are here again, and the timing couldn’t be better, given the state of the drought and our final approach toward the month of June.
• As has been the case for the last several days, we’re starting the day with a firm overcast across the area. It, along with the persistent southerly light to moderate wind overnight, has helped to keep temps in their quite balmy mid-70s.
• As of 7:00 am, we have two areas of rainfall. The first one is more showery and runs between I-35 & I-45. There are a few lightning strikes in there, but they are the exception. It’s associated with a feature centered around Round Rock. The second area of rain is across North Central Oklahoma and stretches down southwest into North Texas, between Wichita Falls and Decatur. That rainfall is associated with a cold front that we’ve been talking about for several days now and is heading in our general direction. 
• As we go through the day, it’ll be the rainfall helped along by that front, which will be our main influence across East Texas. I look for showers and thunderstorms to further organize as we get closer to and especially past lunchtime, as the front makes further southward progress and has the chance to interact with daytime heating. This should result in some strong to potentially severe storms, with wind being the main player this far to the east. That said, there will be some better hail potential well to our west, too. Overall, the tornado risk doesn’t look too high with this event, given the lack of significant shear near the surface. 
• SPC has a broadly drawn “Slight” risk outline that covers all of East Texas today and this evening. In addition, the WPC (Weather Prediction Center) has its own “Slight” risk outline in place for some flooding potential from these expected heavy downpours, too. That covers much of our western counties as well as some of our central counties, and places like Tyler & Jacksonville. 
• Fortunately or unfortunately, depending on how you look at it, our dry soil and this ongoing drought will allow some ability for absorption from heavy rain, at least initially. However, the continuous opportunity for heavy rain going through the weekend will increase that flood potential, and this is going to quickly transition into the main thing we’ll be talking about as the week unfolds.
• Look for showers and thunderstorms to gradually lose composure this evening as daytime heating exits the stage. This should result in an overall lowering of rainfall potential as we go deeper into the night, too. All that to say, we’re not looking at some kind of late-night severe weather episode around these parts.
• The front, which will be a big catalyst for all of this today, will stall somewhere south of I-20 tonight and remain in the area through the day on Thursday in some shape, form, or fashion. It will help to focus additional showers and thunderstorms again on Wednesday afternoon and early evening, then again in even more grand fashion on Thursday as some better support aloft is allowed into the mix. 
• By Friday, that boundary should have washed out for the most part, but the steady southwest flow aloft will still be in here, and it will provide periodic disturbances which should foster better rainfall development at times. Then, there’s the fact that we’ll be open for daily development each afternoon, which will carry over into the evening hours if nothing else through the weekend, with no real limiting factors otherwise present. 
• All this to say, we’re looking at a very wet next 6-7 days, which we desperately need. Temps will be held in check by the presence of the clouds and the rain. However, any breaks in those clouds would obviously allow for a quick localized jump, but I don’t see any significant warmth, per se.
• The Weather Prediction Center is advertising anywhere from 4.5-7” of rain over the course of the next 7 days. Stay tuned… 

☀️ Today • Sunrise: 6:20 am - Sunset: 8:15 pm | Total Daylight: 13:54 (+1:16) ⎥ Tyler Normals: 65/84 – Records: 94°/2020 -- 46°/1976  – 3.97”/2000
  
📊 Lower 48 Temp Extremes for Monday:  109° at Rio Grande Village 🔹 10° at 22 miles southwest of Manila, Utah

• Monday Climate Stats • Tyler City: 77/89 (0) -- Tyler Pounds: 77/91 (0) -- Longview: 74/88 (T) – Lufkin: 76/87 (T) #etxwx #txwx
